newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former head of French Church of Scientology guilty. [CORRECTED]
newsitem.headline: Former head of French Church of Scientology guilty. [CORRECTED]

text.p: A court on Friday convicted Jean-Jacques Mazier, former head of the French Church of Scientology in Lyon, central France (corrects to clarify that Mazier was only head of the church in Lyon), of manslaughter and sentenced him to 18 months in prison with another 18 months suspended.
After an eight-day trial in October, the court convicted 14 other defendants tied to the church on charges ranging from embezzlement to fraud and acquitted eight others.

At the trial in Lyon, central France, prosecutors sought to portray the church as a dangerous religious sect while defence lawyers argued their clients were the innocent victims of a campaign by the centre-right government to crack down on cults.

Public prosecutor Thierry Ricard had asked the court to sentence 21 of the 23 defendants in the dock to suspended jail terms and fines of up to 500,000 francs ($100,000). Apart from Mazier, the 14 others convicted were given suspended sentences.
Mazier was accused of manslaughter and fraud in the 1988 suicide of church follower Patrice Vic, who the prosecution said had been put under duress.

The prosecution said Vic, a 30-year-old industrial designer, threw himself off a high-rise block because he could not raise the cash to attend a scientology course. The defence blamed Vic's suicide on long-term depression and alcohol abuse.
